rounds.fact: WebMD launched in 1996 and became so widely used for self-diagnosis that 'don't WebMD your symptoms' turned into a common joke about people convincing themselves they had rare diseases.

About.com organized the web using human 'guides' who curated links on specific topics, a labor-intensive model for making sense of the internet before search engines got good enough to do it automatically.
Photobucket became the default way millions of MySpace users hosted images for their profiles, since MySpace itself didn't offer easy photo uploading in its early years.
Match.com launched in 1995 and is one of the very first online dating sites, predating the smartphone-app dating era by almost two decades.
Epinions paid ordinary users for writing product reviews, an early attempt to build trust in user opinions before that became a standard feature on almost every shopping site.
